sources.role: Identifies the desktop program and its Thall/Nguyen (2012) method.

Published primary specification: Sections 3–5 give saturated continuation marginals, Gaussian copula, monotone increments, independent normal/truncated-normal priors, allocation criteria and the radiation-therapy example.
Author preprint with legible mathematical text, used to cross-check the published PDF's character encoding.

Original1.8 guide and bounded native reference probes for ordinal marginals, patient likelihood, screening, randomization, cohort bookkeeping, parser spellings and ESS moment reduction. Original assets not redistributed.

implementation_choices: Independent paper-based implementation with efficacy-by-toxicity array axes and zero-based doses/categories.
Logistic continuation probabilities; monotone endpoints use baseline logits plus nonnegative increments. Nonmonotone endpoints use free logits at each dose.
Explicit underlying normal prior means and standard deviations; positive increments have truncated-normal priors. The common Gaussian-copula correlation is uniform on (-1,1) unless explicitly fixed.
The strict toxicity event in equation 6 is used; Section 5's inclusive example differs only at exact equality.
Near-optimality and probability-of-being-best are defined across all doses before safety filtering, following equations 7–9. All tied maxima count toward probability-of-being-best.
Adaptive randomization is proportional to predictive good-outcome probability, not mean utility. No untried dose may be skipped during escalation.

Final selection exposes both an acceptable-set maximum and the literal Section 4.4 global maximum gated by a nonempty acceptable set; the distinction is explicit because these differ when the global best is unsafe.
limitations: Current desktop study import, calibrated priors/ESS integration, calendar conduct/simulation, adaptive precision and native report workflows remain open. Low-level toxicity-only posterior inference is integrated. Source references do not establish native inference/RNG identity or clinical validity.
